# v2.75 — disable an account instead of deleting it

This stable release rolls up dev pre-release **v2.75-dev**.

Until now, the only way to stop someone signing in was to delete their account — which also threw away their login history, their role and their company access. Offboarding a leaver, or suspending an account for a few weeks, shouldn't be a one-way door. It no longer is.

## What's new

**You can disable and re-enable a user account.** In **Admin → Users**, each row has a power icon in the Actions column.

**Disabling takes effect immediately — including for someone already signed in.** They're signed out on their very next click, rather than lingering until their session happens to expire. They then can't sign back in.

**Nothing is lost.** Their role, company access, MFA setup and login history are all kept, so enabling the account later restores it exactly as it was. When you disable someone you can record an optional reason ("Left the company", "On extended leave"); it's shown to other admins in the tooltip on the grey **Disabled** badge beside their role, along with who disabled the account and when. Disabled rows are greyed out so they stand out in the list.

**Guardrails.** You can't disable your own account, and you can't disable the last SuperAdmin — so nobody can accidentally lock everyone out of the admin pages.

**A disabled user gets the ordinary "Invalid username or password" message** when they try to sign in. That's deliberate: a distinct message would confirm to an attacker that the username is real. The attempt still shows up for you in the **Failed login attempts** panel with the reason *Account disabled*.

## Changed

**In the Users table, the MFA column now reads "Off" rather than "Disabled".** With an account-status badge on the same row, two different meanings of "Disabled" read as a contradiction.

## Fixed

**The "last SuperAdmin" protection could be fooled by a disabled SuperAdmin.** The checks that stop you demoting or deleting your final SuperAdmin counted disabled accounts as if they could still administer the system. If your only other SuperAdmin was disabled, the app would let you demote or delete the last usable one — leaving nobody able to reach the admin pages. Both checks now ignore disabled accounts.

**Editing a user no longer returns a server error for an unknown account.** A request naming a user that doesn't exist now returns a clean "not found".

## Notes

- The update applies one database migration, adding three columns to the users table. The update script handles this for you; there is nothing to run by hand. **Every existing account stays enabled.**
- Disabled state is included in backups and survives a restore, so a suspended account comes back suspended.
- Prefer disabling to deleting when someone leaves: deletion is permanent and discards their login history.
